summary.headline: Texmaco Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR753 crore, but PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore on finance cost cuts and a turnaround in Rail Infra.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR753 crore, hit by lower freight car and Rail & Green execution, while Bright Power grew 76.8% YoY to INR175 crore. EBITDA was INR81 crore (10.8% margin), flat YoY, and PBT rose 4.8% YoY to INR44 crore after finance costs fell 18.2% YoY. Order book stood at INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with private and export share of the freight car order book at 96.4% in Q1 FY27. Management tied the lower volume to supply-chain stress linked to high oil and gas prices and guided to better execution from coming quarters.

segments.name: Freight Cars (FCD)
segments.commentary: 1,054 freight cars delivered in Q1 FY27; private and export share of order book rose from 21% in FY25 to 79% in FY26 and 96.4% in Q1 FY27. Orders in hand exceed 6,000 wagons, including South Africa.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Production of 5,148 tons in the quarter.

segments.name: Rail Infra & Green (formerly Kalindee)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY on lower execution; EBIT margin turned positive at 1.4% versus a loss a year ago.

segments.name: Bright Power (Electrical Infra)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR175 crore, up 76.8% YoY; EBIT margin 10.8%, up 150 bps YoY.

segments.name: Leasing JV (Texmaco Touax)
segments.commentary: Trinity entry cuts Texmaco's stake from 50% to 34%; JV sits outside Texmaco's standalone numbers. About 35 rakes currently on lease, with readiness to invest in about 100 more rakes near term.

guidance_outlook: Core business EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% (as stated) over the next 1 to 3 years, with a journey toward mid-teens bottom-line margin.
Vision 2030: double the top line from the current INR5,000-6,000 crore run-rate, adding new businesses, with steady bottom line in the mid-teens.
New businesses could add 20% to 50% top-line growth in a given year; management cited 15% to 20% revenue growth over 1 to 2 years as a reading of its comments.

South Africa order (about INR4,100 crore, wagons plus long-term maintenance): about 50% to 60% expected to be executed in FY28, balance spread over later years; locomotive value to be added once a partner is finalised.
Freight car output expected to improve from coming quarters as supply-chain issues are resolved through alternative arrangements.
capex_capacity: Freight car capacity described as elastic at 15,000-16,000 wagons a year, but management said volume is not the focus.
Considering a locomotive plant and wagon manufacturing plant in South Africa; management declined to confirm the INR200-300 crore investment figure reported in the press.
Leasing JV: near-term readiness to invest in about 100 more rakes; press report of about INR1,800 crore over 3 to 5 years for about 100 trains was not confirmed by management.
Capital allocation to Kavach and defence described as modest in share of total capex.
Qualification work under way for semi high-speed and high-speed passenger rolling stock via Saira Asia (interiors).
demand_pricing: Order book INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with Q1 wins including a South Africa order of about INR4,100 crore (wagons plus 15-year maintenance, maintenance about 30-35% of value).
Management says railways is not yet ordering; near-term order flow expected from private and export customers only.
Supply-chain stress in Q1 linked to high oil and gas prices affecting bogies and other components; wheelset supply from Rail Wheel Factory adequate for now.
Margin improvement attributed to product mix, geographic expansion and AI-enabled efficiency actions; no normalised margin guidance given.
Other expenses rose because freight charges on export wagons are booked there while the related income sits in total revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the reported INR1,800 crore investment for about 100 leasing rakes correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure; leasing JV investment is outside Texmaco's standalone books, and Texmaco's stake falls to 34% after Trinity's entry.

qa_highlights.question: Execution challenges in FCD given 96% private and export order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No execution challenges; Q1 was hit by industry-wide supply-chain stress from high oil and gas prices, with output expected to improve from coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the South Africa order and its revenue timing?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR4,100 crore figure is wagons plus long-term maintenance; about 50% to 60% expected in FY28. Locomotive value is additional and under partner discussion.

qa_highlights.question: FY27/FY28 revenue and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Core EBITDA margin target 1.2% to 3% over 1 to 3 years; new businesses could add 20% to 50% top-line growth in a year; no absolute figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook as order mix shifts to private and export?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance; management said margin improvement is a continuing journey toward positivity.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Indian Railways wagon tender?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects railway demand eventually given National Rail Plan modal share targets, but says Texmaco is currently insulated from it.

risks_watch: Freight car output and execution remain weak; Q1 volume was down and recovery depends on supply-chain normalisation (oil and gas linked stress, bogies, wheelsets).
Revenue concentration in the South Africa order and dependence on private and export demand while railway tenders remain absent.
Locomotive scope for South Africa is undefined; partner tie-up and value still pending.
Management declined to give numerical guidance on FY27/FY28 revenue, EBITDA or margins; watch for formal guidance.
Diversification into defence, Kavach, renewables and metro/Vande Bharat lacks disclosed numbers, capital allocation or returns.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term vision (Texmaco 2.0, Vision 2030) and margin direction, but evasive on specifics: declined to give numbers on South Africa investment, locomotives, leasing capex, defence and FY27 or FY28 guidance.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: South Africa order execution

rows.label: Leasing JV fleet expansion (Texmaco Touax)
rows.why: About 35 rakes on lease now and readiness to invest in about 100 more rakes near term, though the INR1,800 crore figure was not confirmed and Texmaco's stake falls from 50% to 34% after Trinity's entry.

rows.label: Rail Infra & Green turnaround
rows.why: EBIT margin turned positive at 1.4% in Q1 FY27 versus a loss a year ago, with Rail Infra & Green revenue down YoY on lower execution.
